problem: Use a fundamental vector product to determine which of the following integrals gives the surface area generated when the curve $y=\frac{x}{x+1}$ is rotated by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [0,4].$

examples.problem: Use a fundamental vector product to find an integral expression for the surface area generated when the curve $x=\sin z$ is rotated by $2\pi$ radians about the $z$-axis for $z \in [0, \pi].$
examples.worked_solution:
Notice that $x=\sin z \geq 0$ for all $z \in [0, \pi].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(z)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(z)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,(z,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(z)=\sin z,$ and

$$
D = \big\{ (z,\theta) \, : \, 0 \leq z \leq \pi , \, 0 \leq \theta \leq 2\pi\big\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂z},\,\frac{∂y}{∂z},\,\frac{∂z}{∂z}⟩=⟨{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}f{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{f}^{′}f{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}f⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

  

and

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖ & =\sqrt{(-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+({f}^{′}f)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}+{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}} \\  & =f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖\text{d}z\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={∬}_{D}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta \,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\cdot \theta \,{|}_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}z \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(z)=\sin z,$ we obtain $f'(z) = \cos z.$ So, finally, we conclude that our expression for the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡z\sqrt{1+(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)^{2}}\,\text{d}z \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
⟨\,{cos}^{2}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\text{_______}\,,\,{cos}^{2}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

 

The fundamental vector product of the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x={cos}^{2}⁡y$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}]$ is given above. What is the $2$nd  component of the product?
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $x={cos}^{2}⁡y\ge 0$ for all $y\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y,\,f(y)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,(y,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(y)={cos}^{2}⁡y,$ and  

$$
D={(y,\theta )\,:\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le \theta <2\pi }.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂y},\,\frac{∂y}{∂y},\,\frac{∂z}{∂y}⟩=⟨{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,1,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{f}^{′}f{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{f}^{′}f{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{f}^{′}f,\,f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f={cos}^{2}⁡y,$ we obtain ${f}^{′}=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡y.$ So, finally, we conclude that the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}=⟨{cos}^{2}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡y{cos}^{3}⁡y,\,{cos}^{2}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
